# Design system reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm design:docs` from src/design-system/tokens.ts and the usage blocks in src/components/site/*.astro and src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro. Do not edit by hand; `pnpm check` fails when this file is out of date. -->

Read this before building or changing a page. `docs/design-rules.md` holds the rules above the components (where content lives, motion).

## Rules

1. Wrap the page in `BaseLayout`. Build it only from the components below. Put `Split` and `Section` directly inside `BaseLayout`; use `Stack` and `Grid` inside them.
2. Pages never set margin, padding, gap or inset. Components own their spacing. To change space between things, pass a `gap` prop: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` or `xl`.
3. Spacing has five steps: `--space-xs`, `--space-sm`, `--space-md`, `--space-lg`, `--space-xl`. No raw px/rem/em, no clamp()/calc() sizes, no other spacing tokens.
4. Use color, type, corner and border tokens by their role (see "Use for"). Don't invent new values; if something is missing, ask Jaden or a board admin.
5. If no component fits, add a small one in `src/components/site/` with a usage block (copy an existing one), then run `pnpm design:docs`. Keep it to what the page needs.
6. Sanity (through `contentRepository`) holds only content that changes often: events, news, newsletters, notices, hours, fundraisers, site settings. Everything else (service details, prices, fees, About Us, ways to help, page photos) is written in the page file in Figma's wording; never add Sanity fields for it. See docs/design-rules.md.
7. Pages have no `<style>`, `style=` or `class=` of their own, and no raw colors, sizes or spacing. If Figma needs something new, extend a component with a prop or variant (never copy one) or add a reusable one. A Figma value that isn't a token is snapped to the nearest token and listed in the PR.
8. Every page passes BaseLayout its own `title` ("<Page> | Cottonwood Community Library") and `description` (1–2 sentences from facts on the page), and an `image` when it has its own photo. The canonical address, share card, schema.org data and sitemap entry are automatic. See "Search and sharing" in docs/design-rules.md.

Breakpoints used inside components (min-width): tablet `48rem` (768px), split `64rem` (1024px), desktop `90rem` (1440px), wide `100rem` (1600px).

`pnpm check` enforces rules 2, 3 and 7 on `src/styles/base.css`, `BaseLayout.astro`, `src/components/site/*` and every page that imports them, and checks that this file is up to date.

## Tokens

### Colors

Use the role names below. Do not add new colors or shades.

| Token | Value | Use for | Don't use for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-primary` | `#4956a7` | Primary actions (Donate), the opening-hours strip and active accents. | Body text or large backgrounds behind long text. | `background: var(--color-primary);` |
| `--color-primary-ink` | `#1b2040` | Outlined buttons, their labels and borders, badge labels and contact details. | Page background or headings (use --color-text). | `border-color: var(--color-primary-ink);` |
| `--color-primary-soft` | `#e3e7ff` | Panels beside a photo: opening hours, a program or event summary (Split panel). | Buttons, text, or the page background (use --color-background). | `background: var(--color-primary-soft);` |
| `--color-accent` | `#beedae` | Supporting actions (directions, donations) and the notices bar. | Text color; it fails contrast on paper. | `<Button variant="accent">` |
| `--color-accent-ink` | `#3b5c30` | Text and icons on pale-green backgrounds. | Text on paper or white (use --color-text). | `color: var(--color-accent-ink);` |
| `--color-background` | `#f7f8ff` | The page background. | Cards that must stand out from the page (use --color-surface). | `background: var(--color-background);` |
| `--color-surface` | `#ffffff` | Raised surfaces, badges on photos, and text on indigo. | The page background. | `background: var(--color-surface);` |
| `--color-text` | `#000000` | Headings and primary text. | Secondary or supporting copy (use --color-text-muted). | `<Text>` |
| `--color-text-muted` | `#525252` | Supporting text, dates and secondary icons. | Headings, or text under 16px on colored backgrounds. | `<Text tone="muted">` |
| `--color-border` | `#d9d9d9` | Subtle outlines around badges and dividers. | Text or icons; it is too light to read. | `border: var(--border-thin) solid var(--color-border);` |
| `--color-icon-muted` | `#c1c1c1` | Muted icons on the indigo strip. | Anything on a light background. | `color: var(--color-icon-muted);` |

### Fonts

Two self-hosted families. Headings use Bree Serif; everything else uses Mona Sans.

| Token | Value | Use for | Don't use for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--font-display` | `'Bree Serif', Georgia, serif` (Regular · 400) | Page titles and section headings. | Body copy, buttons, labels or card titles. | `<Heading size="display">` |
| `--font-body` | `'Mona Sans Variable', 'Mona Sans', sans-serif` (Medium 500 / Semibold 600 / Bold 700) | Body copy, navigation, links, buttons, dates and labels. | Page and section headings (use --font-display). | `font-family: var(--font-body);` |
| `--weight-regular` | `400` | Bree Serif headings. | Mona Sans text; it is lighter than the design. | `font-weight: var(--weight-regular);` |
| `--weight-medium` | `500` | Body text and opening hours. | Buttons and card titles (use bold). | `font-weight: var(--weight-medium);` |
| `--weight-semibold` | `600` | Navigation and footer links. | Paragraphs. | `font-weight: var(--weight-semibold);` |
| `--weight-bold` | `700` | Buttons, card titles and badges. | Whole paragraphs or Bree Serif headings. | `font-weight: var(--weight-bold);` |

### Type sizes

Body and heading sizes come from the 1920px design and scale down on phones (--fluid-*); Heading and Text pick the right one. Utility is the compact header label size.

| Token | Value | Use for | Don't use for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--text-utility` | `0.9375rem` (15px) | The compact opening-hours strip and short utility labels. | Body copy and main navigation. | `font-size: var(--text-utility);` |
| `--text-label` | `1.25rem` (20px) | Badges, dates and notices. | Paragraphs people need to read. | `<Text size="label">` |
| `--text-body` | `1.5rem` (24px) | Body copy, card titles, navigation and buttons. | Headings. | `<Text>` |
| `--text-lead` | `1.875rem` (30px) | A short introduction under a heading, and the wordmark. | More than two sentences. | `<Text size="lead">` |
| `--text-heading` | `3.125rem` (50px) | Section headings (h2). | Card titles (use <Heading size="title">). | `<Heading size="heading">` |
| `--text-display` | `4.375rem` (70px) | The one main page heading (h1). | More than once per page. | `<Heading level={1} size="display">` |
| `--leading-tight` | `1` | Big headings, badges and the wordmark. | Paragraphs; lines would touch. | `line-height: var(--leading-tight);` |
| `--leading-snug` | `1.25` | Card titles and other short bold text that can wrap. | Paragraphs. | `line-height: var(--leading-snug);` |
| `--leading-relaxed` | `1.5` | Body copy, buttons and centered section headings. | Display headings. | `line-height: var(--leading-relaxed);` |

### Spacing

Five steps, nothing in between. Components apply them; pages choose a step only through a gap prop (xs, sm, md, lg, xl).

| Token | Value | Use for | Don't use for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--space-xs` | `0.625rem` (10px) | Icon + label, buttons side by side, badge padding. | Space between unrelated groups. | `<Stack direction="row" gap="xs">` |
| `--space-sm` | `1.25rem` (20px) | Card title + description, button padding, footer link lists. | Space between page sections. | `<Stack gap="sm">` |
| `--space-md` | `1.875rem` (30px) | Card gutters, heading + text + actions stacks. | Tight icon + label pairs. | `<Grid columns={3} gap="md">` |
| `--space-lg` | `3.75rem` (60px) | Between big groups inside a section; page edges on tablets. | Inside cards or buttons. | `<Stack gap="lg">` |
| `--space-xl` | `6.25rem` (100px) | Section rhythm and page edges on wide screens. | Anything inside a section; it splits content apart. | `padding-block: var(--space-xl);` |

### Layout

Widths cap content. The three responsive spacing aliases step between the 5 spacing values at fixed breakpoints; they never produce other values.

| Token | Value | Use for | Don't use for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--width-content` | `95rem` (1520px) | Max width of section content (card grids). At 1920px this leaves the design’s 200px margins. | Text columns (use --width-copy). | `<Section width="content">` |
| `--width-wide` | `82.5rem` (1320px) | The Find us map (MapCard caps itself at this width). | Text or card grids. | `max-width: var(--width-wide);` |
| `--width-article` | `70rem` (1120px) | A news list or an event’s text and buttons (Figma Events & News, Event View): PostList, Section width="article". | Long text on its own (use --width-text) or card grids. | `<Section width="article">` |
| `--width-copy` | `38.875rem` (622px) | Readable text columns: hero copy, newsletter, split sections. | Card grids. | `<Section width="copy">` |
| `--width-text` | `57.5rem` (920px) | Long reading on its own: FAQs, articles, the About story (Section width="text", Prose). | Text beside a photo (use --width-copy) or card grids. | `<Section width="text">` |
| `--page-inset` | `var(--space-sm)` (20 → 60 → 100px) → `var(--space-lg)` from 48rem, `var(--space-xl)` from 100rem | Left and right space at the page edge. Section, Split, header and footer apply it. | Spacing inside content; pages never need it directly. | `padding-inline: var(--page-inset);` |
| `--section-space` | `var(--space-lg)` (60 → 100px) → `var(--space-xl)` from 100rem | Space above and below each page section. Section and Split apply it. | Gaps inside a section (use --section-gap). | `padding-block: var(--section-space);` |
| `--section-gap` | `var(--space-lg)` (60 → 30 → 60px) → `var(--space-md)` from 48rem, `var(--space-lg)` from 100rem | Space between a section’s heading, content and action. Section applies it by default. Phones get the large step: their cards stack (60px apart), so a heading or button closer than that reads as part of the nearest card. | Space inside cards or between buttons. | `gap: var(--section-gap);` |

### Corners

Three shapes only.

| Token | Value | Use for | Don't use for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--radius-none` | `0px` | Sections, strips and edges where a photo bleeds off the page. | Photos inside the page (use --radius-image). | `border-radius: var(--radius-none);` |
| `--radius-image` | `2.1875rem` (35px) | Photos, image containers and floating panels. | Buttons and badges (use --radius-pill). | `border-radius: var(--radius-image);` |
| `--radius-pill` | `6.25rem` (100px) | Buttons, badges and contact strips. | Photos or large panels. | `<Button> / <Badge>` |

### Borders

Use with a solid style and a color token. The underline tokens set how thick link underlines are and how far below the text they sit.

| Token | Value | Use for | Don't use for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--border-thin` | `1px` | Outlined buttons, badges and photo edges. | Focus outlines (base.css handles focus). | `border: var(--border-thin) solid var(--color-border);` |
| `--border-strong` | `2px` | Filled buttons, so they match outlined ones in size. | Decorative frames. | `border: var(--border-strong) solid var(--color-primary);` |
| `--underline-thickness` | `0.12em` (about 3px on body text) | Every underlined link. base.css sets it on all links; switch underlines on with text-decoration-line: underline (the text-decoration shorthand resets it). | Borders, dividers or focus outlines (use --border-thin / base.css). | `text-decoration-thickness: var(--underline-thickness);` |
| `--underline-offset` | `0.25em` | Space between a link’s text and its underline, so the thicker line clears letters like g and y. | Spacing between elements (use the spacing steps). | `text-underline-offset: var(--underline-offset);` |

### Photo edges

A small color inset shared by photo frames. Keep logos, printed pages and contained artwork plain. Reverse the offset on photos that bleed off the right page edge.

| Token | Value | Use for | Don't use for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--shadow-photo` | `.25rem .375rem 0 var(--color-primary-soft)` | Split photos, photo cards and gallery frames. | Logos, printed pages, text and controls. | `box-shadow: var(--shadow-photo);` |
| `--shadow-photo-reverse` | `-.25rem .375rem 0 var(--color-accent)` | Right-bleeding photos including the hero, and alternating photo cards. | Logos, printed pages, text and controls. | `box-shadow: var(--shadow-photo-reverse);` |

### Motion

CSS speeds for hover and press feedback. Entrances and sliding (sections rising in, FAQ answers) use Motion springs in src/scripts/motion.ts through data-motion; see docs/design-rules.md, Motion. Nothing loops or waits, and everything is off for visitors who ask for reduced motion.

| Token | Value | Use for | Don't use for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--motion-quick` | `150ms` | Hover and press feedback: button colors, arrows nudging, a button pressing in. | Anything that opens or moves into place (use --motion-smooth). | `transition: background-color var(--motion-quick) var(--ease-out);` |
| `--motion-smooth` | `300ms` | CSS changes that move a little further: the icon turning in the phone menu button, a card photo zooming, the FAQ + turning into ×. | Hover colors; they feel sluggish (use --motion-quick). | `transition: transform var(--motion-smooth) var(--ease-out);` |
| `--motion-entrance` | `600ms` | A slower CSS change the visitor watches happen once. | Entrances (use data-motion, src/scripts/motion.ts) or anything the visitor clicked; they would wait for it. | `animation: rise var(--motion-entrance) var(--ease-out) both;` |
| `--ease-out` | `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` | Every transition and animation: starts quickly, settles gently. | Linear or bouncy curves; they read as mechanical or playful. | `transition-timing-function: var(--ease-out);` |

## Components

Import from `src/components/site/` (BaseLayout from `src/layouts/`). Each component's usage block in its file is the source for this section.

| Component | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [BaseLayout](#baselayout) | The page shell for every page: fonts, tokens, notices, header, footer, analytics and the skip link. |
| [Badge](#badge) | Small pill label: a date, a status, or a short link to a campaign. |
| [BookUnderline](#bookunderline) | A short indigo pencil stroke ending in an open book, below a single heading line. |
| [Button](#button) | Pill-shaped call to action. A link when given `href`, otherwise a button element. |
| [Card](#card) | Photo card with a title and a short description. With `href` the whole card is one link: click anywhere on it, only the title underlines, and the focus ring goes around the whole card. Use inside a Grid. |
| [DetailList](#detaillist) | Rows of a label on the left and a value on the right, with a thin line between rows: opening hours, prices. |
| [EventCards](#eventcards) | The next upcoming events as Cards with date badges, then regular programs (Story Time, reading groups) to fill any of the `limit` spots left. Built ahead of time, so the visitor's browser hides events after they end, keeps `limit` cards showing, and swaps dates for "Today", "Tomorrow" and "This Friday". The layout follows how many are showing: 1 is one wide card (photo beside text), 2 are centered, 3 or more fill the grid, 0 shows `emptyMessage`. Events with no photo of their own or of their program get a library photo picked by event id, never the hero photo, and never one another card already shows. Regular programs show their next date ("Nov 4 · 11:30 a.m.") worked out from their schedule text; a schedule it can't read shows as written. |
| [Faq](#faq) | Questions that open to show their answer, with a + that turns into ×. Only one is open at a time (details name=…; with JavaScript the script does it, so both answers can slide). Works without JavaScript (details/summary). |
| [FundraiserForm](#fundraiserform) | The active fundraiser's Givebutter Form widget: live goal bar and the donation form, right on the page (at #give). Without JavaScript, or until Givebutter's script loads, a link to the fundraiser's Givebutter page shows instead. |
| [Gallery](#gallery) | A grid of rounded photos with their captions (if any): the About gallery, the founders' pair, photos from an event. |
| [Grid](#grid) | Equal-width columns that collapse to one column on phones. |
| [Heading](#heading) | Page and section headings in Bree Serif, plus bold card-style titles. |
| [IconLink](#iconlink) | A text link with an icon before or after it, underlined on hover. |
| [LibraryIllustration](#libraryillustration) | Transparent crayon scenes with enough presence to anchor a heading, using the library's indigo and green palette. |
| [MapCard](#mapcard) | The library on a map, with the address and phone number as pills on its top edge (Figma "Find us"). The map loads when it scrolls into view; without it (no network, no WebGL) the address and a directions link show instead. |
| [PageTitle](#pagetitle) | The page's opening title (h1), optional topic artwork, breadcrumbs, and one muted supporting line such as an event's date. Illustrated index titles put the artwork on the right on desktop and above the title on phones. |
| [PostList](#postlist) | News posts as rows: photo on the left; date, title, summary and "Read more" on the right (Figma "Latest News"). Shows the newest few; "Load more news" reveals the rest (all show without JavaScript). |
| [Prose](#prose) | Longer reading text: paragraphs, subheadings (h2/h3), lists and links, from Sanity rich text, plain paragraphs, or (for site policies kept in code, like Privacy) the slot. Large muted text as on the About and event pages. |
| [Section](#section) | One full-width band of the page: page-edge inset, vertical rhythm, an optional heading, and its content stacked below. |
| [Signature](#signature) | A sign-off: a muted thank-you line, then the small tree logo beside the two-line library name (Figma About Us "Thank you for your support!"). |
| [Split](#split) | A large photo beside a text column. The photo bleeds off one page edge at every width; on phones and tablets it sits above the text, a little taller (3:2) so it isn't a thin strip. With `panel` the text sits on a pale-indigo panel that runs off the other edge (Visit Us hours). With `inset` both stay inside the content width and the photo is rounded on every corner (Explore Services). |
| [Stack](#stack) | Puts children in a column (or a row) with one of the 5 gaps between them. |
| [Text](#text) | A paragraph (or inline text) in one of the body sizes and tones. |
| [TopicList](#topiclist) | Short topics, each a bold sub-heading over a muted paragraph (Figma Explore Services "Getting started" / "Renewals & returns"). |
| [WideImage](#wideimage) | One large rounded photo across the page, right under the page title (Figma Event View and About Us). |

### BaseLayout

`src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro` — The page shell for every page: fonts, tokens, notices, header, footer, analytics and the skip link.

- **Use for:** Wrapping every page. Put Splits and Sections directly inside it. Every page passes its own `title` ("<Page> | Cottonwood Community Library") and `description` (1–2 sentences from facts on the page), and an `image` when it has its own photo. Canonical address, share card, schema.org data and the sitemap entry are automatic (docs/design-rules.md, "Search and sharing").
- **Don't use for:** Page-level styles or spacing: build from src/components/site instead. Reusing another page's title or description.

```ts
interface Props {
  /** Browser tab, search and share-card title, unique to this page: "<Page> | Cottonwood Community Library". */
  title: string;
  /** 1–2 sentences for search results and share cards, from facts on this page. Unique to this page. */
  description: string;
  /** Photo for the link preview on Facebook and in texts; the homepage photo when absent. Pass the page's own photo. */
  image?: LibraryImage;
  /** 'article' for a news post. */
  type?: 'website' | 'article';
  /** Extra schema.org data for search engines and AI answers (src/content/seo.mjs). */
  schema?: Record<string, unknown>[];
  /** Keep this page out of search results (the "page not found" page). */
  noindex?: boolean;
}
```

```astro
<BaseLayout title="Visit | Cottonwood Community Library" description="Hours, directions and services.">
  <Section title="Visit us" headingId="visit-heading">…</Section>
</BaseLayout>
```

### Badge

`src/components/site/Badge.astro` — Small pill label: a date, a status, or a short link to a campaign.

- **Use for:** Short labels of one to five words: event dates, "Fundraiser", a campaign link above the hero heading.
- **Don't use for:** Actions people should click first (use Button), sentences, or lists of tags.

```ts
interface Props {
  /** Makes the badge a link. */
  href?: string;
  /** Render as <time> with this datetime instead of span. */
  datetime?: string;
  /** White fill, for badges on top of photos. */
  surface?: boolean;
  /** Muted icon after the label. */
  iconEnd?: IconName;
  [data: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined;
}
```

```astro
<Badge href="/donate/" iconEnd="external">
  <Image slot="start" image={campaign.image} alt="" width={50} height={50} />
  {campaign.title}
</Badge>
```

### BookUnderline

`src/components/site/BookUnderline.astro` — A short indigo pencil stroke ending in an open book, below a single heading line.

- **Use for:** Once in the homepage hero, around the complete second heading line from the CMS.
- **Don't use for:** Repeating the accent on section headings or placing it behind letters.

```astro
<BookUnderline>Your library.</BookUnderline>
```

### Button

`src/components/site/Button.astro` — Pill-shaped call to action. A link when given `href`, otherwise a button element.

- **Use for:** Main actions in a section: directions, donate, volunteer, "Read more", "View all".
- **Don't use for:** Links inside a sentence (use a plain link), card titles (Card links them), or menus.

```ts
interface Props extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<'a'>, 'class' | 'style' | 'type'> {
  href?: string;
  /** outline (default): quiet. accent: pale green, supporting. primary: indigo, one per view. */
  variant?: 'outline' | 'accent' | 'primary';
  /** Icon before the label. */
  icon?: IconName;
  /** Icon after the label (usually "arrow"). */
  iconEnd?: IconName;
  /** Only for <button>. */
  type?: 'button' | 'submit';
  /** Extra words only screen readers and search engines hear, so a short label like "Read more" says where it goes. */
  screenReaderText?: string;
}
```

```astro
<Stack direction="row" gap="xs" wrap>
  <Button href={library.directionsUrl} variant="accent" icon="navigate">Get directions</Button>
  <Button href="/visit/" iconEnd="arrow" screenReaderText="about visiting">Read more</Button>
</Stack>
```

### Card

`src/components/site/Card.astro` — Photo card with a title and a short description. With `href` the whole card is one link: click anywhere on it, only the title underlines, and the focus ring goes around the whole card. Use inside a Grid.

- **Use for:** A set of similar things: events, services, programs, news posts. Three per row on desktop. layout="adaptive" when a card may end up alone in a full-width row (EventCards does this). shape="page" for a printed page such as a newsletter cover: shown whole, at letter size.
- **Don't use for:** A single highlighted item that is always on its own (use Split), text without a photo, a description longer than two lines (it is cut off), or links and buttons inside the card (the card is already one link; a badge must not have href).

```ts
interface Props {
  title: string;
  /** Makes the whole card one link (the title is the link text). */
  href?: string;
  image: LibraryImage;
  /** Use "li" when the parent Grid is as="ul". */
  as?: 'article' | 'li' | 'div';
  /** stacked (default): photo above text. adaptive: photo beside text whenever the card is at least 48rem (768px) wide, e.g. alone in a row. */
  layout?: 'stacked' | 'adaptive';
  /** photo (default): a 3:2 photo on mobile, fixed height on desktop. page: a letter-size page (8.5 × 11), e.g. a newsletter cover, shown whole. */
  shape?: 'photo' | 'page';
  /** Shows the picture as a logo: smaller, centered, with white space around it (sponsor and partner logos). */
  logo?: boolean;
  /** Shows the whole description instead of cutting it at two lines. Use when the card has no page with the full text. */
  fullText?: boolean;
  /** Soft offset edges on photo cards. Logos and printed-page cards always retain their plain frames. */
  crayon?: boolean;
  hidden?: boolean;
  [data: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined;
}
```

```astro
<Grid as="ul" columns={3}>
  <Card as="li" title="Computers & Wi-Fi" href="/visit/#computers" image={photo}>Public computers and Wi-Fi.</Card>
</Grid>
```

### DetailList

`src/components/site/DetailList.astro` — Rows of a label on the left and a value on the right, with a thin line between rows: opening hours, prices.

- **Use for:** Opening hours (inside a Split panel) and price lists such as printing costs. Values that mean "not available" (Closed) pass `muted`.
- **Don't use for:** Long text in either column (use Text or Faq), or rows of links.

```ts
interface Props {
  items: { label: string; value: string; muted?: boolean }[];
  /** Accessible name for the list, e.g. "Opening hours". */
  label?: string;
}
```

```astro
<DetailList items={library.hours.map(row => ({ label: row.days, value: row.hours, muted: /^closed$/i.test(row.hours) }))} />
```

### EventCards

`src/components/site/EventCards.astro` — The next upcoming events as Cards with date badges, then regular programs (Story Time, reading groups) to fill any of the `limit` spots left. Built ahead of time, so the visitor's browser hides events after they end, keeps `limit` cards showing, and swaps dates for "Today", "Tomorrow" and "This Friday". The layout follows how many are showing: 1 is one wide card (photo beside text), 2 are centered, 3 or more fill the grid, 0 shows `emptyMessage`. Events with no photo of their own or of their program get a library photo picked by event id, never the hero photo, and never one another card already shows. Regular programs show their next date ("Nov 4 · 11:30 a.m.") worked out from their schedule text; a schedule it can't read shows as written.

- **Use for:** Any page that lists upcoming events. Pass the events from contentRepository.getEvents().
- **Don't use for:** Past events or news posts (use Grid + Card), or wrapping it in another Grid.

```ts
interface Props {
  events: LibraryEvent[];
  /** Regular programs. They give events their photo and fill spots no dated event takes. */
  programs?: Program[];
  /** How many cards to show. */
  limit?: number;
  /** Shown when there are no upcoming events. */
  emptyMessage?: string;
  /** Fill spots no dated event takes with regular programs. Turn off where the page lists the programs itself. */
  fill?: boolean;
}
```

```astro
<EventCards events={events} programs={programs} limit={3} />
```

### Faq

`src/components/site/Faq.astro` — Questions that open to show their answer, with a + that turns into ×. Only one is open at a time (details name=…; with JavaScript the script does it, so both answers can slide). Works without JavaScript (details/summary).

- **Use for:** "Frequently Asked Questions" on Visit Us, Explore Services and service pages, inside a Section with width="text". Each page asks its own questions: borrowing (Sanity) on Explore Services, visiting on Visit Us, the program on its service page.
- **Don't use for:** Content everyone needs to see without clicking (hours, prices), or a single question (use Heading + Text).

```ts
interface Props {
  items: { question: string; answer: string }[];
  /** Open the first question, as in Figma. */
  openFirst?: boolean;
  /** The library's email: adds "Still have a question? Email us." under the questions. */
  email?: string;
}
```

```astro
<Section title="Frequently Asked Questions" headingId="faq-heading" width="text">
  <Faq items={borrowing} email={library.email} />
</Section>
```

### FundraiserForm

`src/components/site/FundraiserForm.astro` — The active fundraiser's Givebutter Form widget: live goal bar and the donation form, right on the page (at #give). Without JavaScript, or until Givebutter's script loads, a link to the fundraiser's Givebutter page shows instead.

- **Use for:** Only on Support Us (/donate/), inside the fundraiser's Split. Pass the campaign from activeCampaign().
- **Don't use for:** Other pages (use a Donate Button with checkoutAttributes, which opens the same checkout as a popup), or typing totals by hand: the total always comes from Givebutter.

```ts
interface Props { campaign: FundraisingCampaign; }
```

```astro
<FundraiserForm campaign={campaign} />
```

### Gallery

`src/components/site/Gallery.astro` — A grid of rounded photos with their captions (if any): the About gallery, the founders' pair, photos from an event.

- **Use for:** Two or more photos that belong together, inside a Section. Photos come from the page (or Sanity, for news posts); every photo needs real alt text.
- **Don't use for:** A single photo (use WideImage or Split), or photos that need a title and description each (use Card).

```ts
interface Props {
  images: LibraryImage[];
  /** Columns from tablet width up. Phones get one column. */
  columns?: 2 | 3;
}
```

```astro
<Section title="Gallery" headingId="gallery-heading"><Gallery images={story.gallery} /></Section>
```

### Grid

`src/components/site/Grid.astro` — Equal-width columns that collapse to one column on phones.

- **Use for:** Rows of Cards, or any set of same-sized items. In three columns a short last row (one or two items) is centered.
- **Don't use for:** A photo next to text (use Split), or rows of buttons (use Stack direction="row").

```ts
interface Props {
  /** Columns from tablet width (768px) up. Phones always get one column. */
  columns?: 2 | 3 | 4;
  gap?: Space;
  /** Use "ul" when the children are a list (then give each child as="li"). */
  as?: 'div' | 'ul';
  /** Center a short last row in three columns (default). EventCards turns this off and lays out its own rows. */
  balance?: boolean;
  hidden?: boolean;
  [data: `data-${string}`]: string | boolean | undefined;
}
```

```astro
<Grid as="ul" columns={3} gap="md">
  {services.map(service => <Card as="li" title={service.title} image={service.image}>{service.description}</Card>)}
</Grid>
```

### Heading

`src/components/site/Heading.astro` — Page and section headings in Bree Serif, plus bold card-style titles.

- **Use for:** The page's one h1 (size="display"), section headings (size="heading"), small bold titles (size="title").
- **Don't use for:** Making text big for emphasis, or skipping levels (h1 then h3).

```ts
interface Props {
  level?: 1 | 2 | 3;
  /** display: 70px h1. heading: 50px section heading. title: bold body-size title. */
  size?: 'display' | 'heading' | 'title';
  id?: string;
  /** Relaxed line height, for headings centered above a grid. */
  relaxed?: boolean;
}
```

```astro
<Heading level={1} size="display" id="welcome-heading">Your community.<br />Your library.</Heading>
```

### IconLink

`src/components/site/IconLink.astro` — A text link with an icon before or after it, underlined on hover.

- **Use for:** Contact details (address, phone, email), "Library catalog ↗" style links.
- **Don't use for:** Main actions (use Button) or links inside a sentence (use a plain link).

```ts
interface Props extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<'a'>, 'class' | 'style'> {
  href: string;
  /** Icon before the text. */
  icon?: IconName;
  /** Icon after the text, in a muted color. */
  iconEnd?: IconName;
}
```

```astro
<IconLink href={library.phoneHref} icon="phone">{library.phone}</IconLink>
```

### LibraryIllustration

`src/components/site/LibraryIllustration.astro` — Transparent crayon scenes with enough presence to anchor a heading, using the library's indigo and green palette.

- **Use for:** Above a related heading: community for the support block, reading for events, computers for services, books for the newsletter.
- **Don't use for:** Replacing real library photos, overlapping text or controls, or repeating a scene in the same section.

```ts
interface Props {
  scene: 'reading' | 'computers' | 'books' | 'community';
  /** Follow the left edge of a text column, or center above a section heading (default). */
  align?: 'start' | 'center';
  /** Smaller artwork in a supporting text column. */
  size?: 'standard' | 'small';
}
```

```astro
<LibraryIllustration scene="reading" />
```

### MapCard

`src/components/site/MapCard.astro` — The library on a map, with the address and phone number as pills on its top edge (Figma "Find us"). The map loads when it scrolls into view; without it (no network, no WebGL) the address and a directions link show instead.

- **Use for:** The "Find us" section on Visit Us, service pages and event pages: <Section title="Find us"><MapCard library={library} /></Section>.
- **Don't use for:** More than one per page (the map is heavy), or as the only way to show the address.

```ts
interface Props { library: HomeContent['library']; }
```

```astro
<Section title="Find us" headingId="map-heading"><MapCard library={library} /></Section>
```

### PageTitle

`src/components/site/PageTitle.astro` — The page's opening title (h1), optional topic artwork, breadcrumbs, and one muted supporting line such as an event's date. Illustrated index titles put the artwork on the right on desktop and above the title on phones.

- **Use for:** The first block of every page except the homepage. Put it directly inside BaseLayout, before the first Split or Section. Give `trail` only on pages under a top-level page (a service, an event, a news post).
- **Don't use for:** The homepage (its h1 is in the hero), section headings (use Section's title), or more than one per page.

```ts
interface Props {
  /** The page title (the page's one h1). */
  title: string;
  /** Topic artwork for a main index page. Leave article, event-detail and legal titles plain. */
  illustration?: 'reading' | 'computers' | 'books' | 'community';
  /** Pages above this one, after Home. Leave out on top-level pages: the header shows where you are. */
  trail?: NavLink[];
  /** id for the h1. */
  headingId?: string;
}
```

```astro
<PageTitle title={event.title} trail={[{ label: 'Events & News', href: '/events/' }]}>
  <time datetime={event.startsAt}>{date}</time>
</PageTitle>
```

### PostList

`src/components/site/PostList.astro` — News posts as rows: photo on the left; date, title, summary and "Read more" on the right (Figma "Latest News"). Shows the newest few; "Load more news" reveals the rest (all show without JavaScript).

- **Use for:** The news list on Events & News. Pass the posts from contentRepository; they are sorted newest first here.
- **Don't use for:** Events (use EventCards), or a short "latest news" teaser of one item (use Split).

```ts
interface Props {
  posts: LibraryPost[];
  /** How many show before "Load more news". */
  initial?: number;
}
```

```astro
<Section title="Latest News" headingId="news-heading"><PostList posts={posts} /></Section>
```

### Prose

`src/components/site/Prose.astro` — Longer reading text: paragraphs, subheadings (h2/h3), lists and links, from Sanity rich text, plain paragraphs, or (for site policies kept in code, like Privacy) the slot. Large muted text as on the About and event pages.

- **Use for:** Article bodies (news posts, event descriptions), the About story, the privacy notice. Put it in a Section with width="text" and align="start".
- **Don't use for:** Short introductions (use Text), text beside a photo (use Split), or hand-written facts.

```ts
interface Props {
  /** Sanity rich text. */
  blocks?: RichTextBlock[];
  /** Plain paragraphs, when the content has no rich text. */
  paragraphs?: string[];
  /** Numbered steps after the text (how to give books, how to volunteer). */
  steps?: string[];
}
```

```astro
<Section width="text" align="start"><Prose blocks={post.body} /></Section>
<Section width="text" align="start"><Prose paragraphs={story.paragraphs} /></Section>
```

### Section

`src/components/site/Section.astro` — One full-width band of the page: page-edge inset, vertical rhythm, an optional heading, and its content stacked below.

- **Use for:** Every top-level block of a page that isn't a photo-beside-text block (use Split for those).
- **Don't use for:** Nesting Sections, or wrapping a Split in a Section. Inside a Section use Stack and Grid.

```ts
interface Props {
  /** Section heading (h2). Leave out and put your own Heading in the slot if you need markup inside it. */
  title?: string;
  /** A centered crayon scene above the heading, kept in the layout so it cannot cover content. */
  illustration?: 'reading' | 'computers' | 'books' | 'community';
  /** id for the heading; the section is labelled by it. */
  headingId?: string;
  /** center: heading and items centered (default). start: left-aligned. */
  align?: 'center' | 'start';
  /** content: up to 1520px (default). full: the whole width inside the page inset (Figma About Us gallery). article: 1120px (an event's text, a news list). text: a 920px column for FAQs and articles. copy: a 622px column. */
  width?: 'content' | 'full' | 'article' | 'text' | 'copy';
  /** Space between heading, content and actions. Defaults to the responsive section gap (20/30/60px). */
  gap?: Space;
  /** Continues the block above (Service View's line under its photo): no space on top, only the block's own space below. */
  continues?: boolean;
  id?: string;
}
```

```astro
<Section title="Library services" headingId="services-heading">
  <Grid as="ul" columns={3}>…</Grid>
  <Button href="/visit/" iconEnd="arrow">Read more</Button>
</Section>
```

### Signature

`src/components/site/Signature.astro` — A sign-off: a muted thank-you line, then the small tree logo beside the two-line library name (Figma About Us "Thank you for your support!").

- **Use for:** The end of a long text such as the About Us story, inside the same Section as the Prose, before its Donate button.
- **Don't use for:** Page headers or footers (they have their own logo), or more than one per page.

```astro
<Signature>Thank you for your support!</Signature>
```

### Split

`src/components/site/Split.astro` — A large photo beside a text column. The photo bleeds off one page edge at every width; on phones and tablets it sits above the text, a little taller (3:2) so it isn't a thin strip. With `panel` the text sits on a pale-indigo panel that runs off the other edge (Visit Us hours). With `inset` both stay inside the content width and the photo is rounded on every corner (Explore Services).

- **Use for:** The opening hero, a featured event, a call to give or volunteer, opening hours beside a photo (panel), one service described beside its photo (inset). At most one in a row, alternating media="end"/"start".
- **Don't use for:** Several similar items (use Grid + Card), or photos that must not be cropped: every photo fills its frame, posters too (use Gallery to show a whole picture).

```ts
interface Props {
  image: LibraryImage;
  /** Which side the photo is on from desktop width up. */
  media?: 'start' | 'end';
  /** Photo aspect ratio. With `panel` the photo also grows to the panel's height. */
  ratio?: '1314 / 652' | '16 / 9' | '5 / 4';
  /** Text on a pale-indigo panel (--color-primary-soft) that runs off the page edge opposite the photo. */
  panel?: boolean;
  /** Keep photo and text inside the content width (1520px); the photo is rounded on every corner. */
  inset?: boolean;
  /** Soft offset photo edges, including the framed hero. Disable for an intentionally plain block. */
  crayon?: boolean;
  /** id of the heading inside, which labels the section. */
  headingId?: string;
  /** The first block on the page: less space above, and the photo loads immediately. */
  first?: boolean;
  /** id on the section, for links like /services/#computers. */
  id?: string;
  /** id on the photo wrapper, for links like /#visit. */
  mediaId?: string;
  hidden?: boolean;
  [data: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined;
}
```

```astro
<Split media="start" image={photo} headingId="community-heading">
  <Heading id="community-heading">Keep your library open.</Heading>
  <Text tone="muted">No county or taxpayer funding.</Text>
  <Stack direction="row" gap="xs" wrap><Button href="/donate/" variant="accent" icon="heart">Donate</Button></Stack>
</Split>
```

### Stack

`src/components/site/Stack.astro` — Puts children in a column (or a row) with one of the 5 gaps between them.

- **Use for:** Heading + text + buttons, a row of buttons, any simple list of blocks.
- **Don't use for:** Columns of cards (use Grid), or adding space with empty elements or margins.

```ts
interface Props {
  /** Space between children. */
  gap?: Space;
  direction?: 'column' | 'row';
  /** Cross-axis alignment. "stretch" makes column children full width. */
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch';
  /** Rows only: let children wrap to the next line. */
  wrap?: boolean;
  as?: 'div' | 'ul' | 'ol' | 'nav' | 'p';
  id?: string;
}
```

```astro
<Stack gap="md" align="start">
  <Heading size="heading">Keep your library open.</Heading>
  <Text tone="muted">Donations help cover day-to-day operations.</Text>
</Stack>
```

### Text

`src/components/site/Text.astro` — A paragraph (or inline text) in one of the body sizes and tones.

- **Use for:** Introductions, descriptions, dates, small print, an italic side note (`note`).
- **Don't use for:** Headings (use Heading) or text inside Button, Badge and Card, which style their own text.

```ts
interface Props {
  /** muted: graphite, for supporting text. */
  tone?: 'default' | 'muted';
  /** label: 20px. body: 24px (default). lead: 30px. All scale down on phones. */
  size?: 'label' | 'body' | 'lead';
  as?: 'p' | 'span' | 'div';
  /** Italic, for a side note such as "Late fees: 10¢/day, up to the replacement cost." */
  note?: boolean;
  /** Even line lengths for a short introduction, avoiding a single trailing word. */
  balance?: boolean;
}
```

```astro
<Text tone="muted" size="lead">{featured.summary}</Text>
```

### TopicList

`src/components/site/TopicList.astro` — Short topics, each a bold sub-heading over a muted paragraph (Figma Explore Services "Getting started" / "Renewals & returns").

- **Use for:** Two to four sub-topics inside a Split or Section, under that block's Heading: how to get started, renewals, connecting to Wi-Fi.
- **Don't use for:** Questions people click to open (use Faq), label-and-value rows such as prices or hours (use DetailList), or a single paragraph (use Text).

```ts
interface Props {
  items: { title: string; text: string }[];
  /** Heading level of each sub-heading: 3 under a section's h2 (default), 4 under an h3. */
  level?: 3 | 4;
}
```

```astro
<TopicList items={[
  { title: 'Getting started', text: 'Bring photo ID and proof of residence.' },
  { title: 'Renewals & returns', text: 'Renew items up to two times, in person or by phone.' },
]} />
```

### WideImage

`src/components/site/WideImage.astro` — One large rounded photo across the page, right under the page title (Figma Event View and About Us).

- **Use for:** The main photo of an event, news post or the About page. `bleed` lets it run off the right edge at every width, as on About Us.
- **Don't use for:** Photos beside text (use Split), several photos (use Gallery), or logos and posters that must not be cropped.

```ts
interface Props {
  image: LibraryImage;
  /** Run off the right page edge (About Us). */
  bleed?: boolean;
  /** Directly under the page title: less space above, and the photo loads immediately. */
  first?: boolean;
}
```

```astro
<PageTitle title={event.title} />
<WideImage image={event.image} first />
```

### Added by BaseLayout

Pages never place these; they are listed so you know they exist.

- **NewsletterForm** (`src/components/site/NewsletterForm.astro`): The library's own newsletter sign-up form, as in Figma: an email field with a Sign up button beside it. It posts to /api/newsletter, which adds the person to the library's Givebutter mailing list; it works with or without JavaScript and offers an email link if sign-up fails. Don't: A second sign-up form on the same page (the result messages use fixed ids), or Givebutter's signup widget.
- **NewsletterNote** (`src/components/site/NewsletterNote.astro`): A folded-paper newsletter signup with the book-carrying child peeking over its top edge. Don't: Additional forms, decoration behind text, or clipping the form's focus outlines and result messages.
- **SiteFooter** (`src/components/site/SiteFooter.astro`): Newsletter sign-up, then the footer with links, contact details, social icons and the Privacy links. Don't: Adding another newsletter form or contact block to a page.
- **SiteHeader** (`src/components/site/SiteHeader.astro`): Opening-hours strip, then the header bar (logo, main navigation, Donate button, phone menu), which sticks to the top while the strip scrolls away. Don't: Adding a second header or navigation to a page.
- **SiteNotices** (`src/components/site/SiteNotices.astro`): Green bar of current notices (closures, schedule changes) above the header, from the Sanity notice records. Don't: Hard-coding announcements into a page.
